s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Marked swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Presented with blurred vision in the right eye
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity was 20/25 OU
Right eye had full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Normal fundus and visual function in the left eye
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
Immunohistochemistry was positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and other markers

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Marked swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Presented with blurred vision in the right eye
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity was 20/25 OU
Right eye had full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Normal fundus and visual function in the left eye
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
Immunohistochemistry was positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and other markers

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with blurred vision, relative afferent pupillary defect, and mild swelling of the optic disc, followed by sudden vision loss and marked swelling of the optic disc, is consistent with optic neuropathy. The MRI findings of focal enhancement along the enlarged right optic nerve and the vitreous biopsy showing an astrocytic neoplasm also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: central retinal artery occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient did develop occlusion of the central retinal artery, this appears to be a secondary event following the initial optic neuropathy.

rejected.label: central retinal vein occlusion
rejected.why: Similar to central retinal artery occlusion, this condition developed later in the course of the disease and is not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: retinal hemorrhages
rejected.why: Retinal hemorrhages were present, but they are not the primary cause of the patient's vision loss and are more likely a consequence of the underlying optic neuropathy.

rejected.label: arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: There is no indication of arteritis, such as elevated inflammatory markers or a history of giant cell arteritis, to support this diagnosis.
